## Schedule a delivery, then reset it {#delivery-lifecycle}

The site is evergreen between deliveries. Scheduling one is a three-step edit; resetting after one is a four-step export.

**Scheduling.**

- [ ] Fill the `delivery:` block in `_variables.yml` (date, venue/platform, event, mode, registration URL) and set `active: 'true'`. Re-render and push; the landing page grows a "Next delivery" callout. Set `active: 'false'` again afterwards.
- [ ] Decide the extended-universe option at **T-2 weeks** against the go/no-go checklist in `_planning/extended-universe-spec.md`. If GO, the opt-in text there goes into the joining email.
- [ ] Decide recording. If recording: talk segments only, announced at the start of each recorded stretch, paused for hands-on and chat-heavy segments. Nothing in the day depends on the recording either way.
- [ ] Optionally create the prereg mirror form from `_planning/prereg-form-spec.md` and paste its URL into `_variables.yml`. The rendered declaration block is the primary record; the form is a silent secondary. Skipping it costs nothing.

**Resetting, before the next one.**

- [ ] Export the responses Sheet (File → Download → CSV) and commit it as a date-stamped snapshot (e.g. `data/class_results_2026-06-16.csv`); refresh `data/class_results.csv` per `facilitator/live-results-setup.md` if you want the archived cohort visible on the evergreen site.
- [ ] Clear (or archive to a second tab) the old rows in the live Sheet so the next cohort's chart opens near-empty. **Do not touch the Form, the Worker, or the field schema** – the pipeline is working; only the rows rotate.

---

## The week before

- [ ] Click once through the Block 3 tab choreography (deck → the spec-menu page → the results page and back) so the switching order is in your fingers – it is the one sequence the day performs live several times.
- [ ] Send joining instructions: setup page link (two routes), the two-window/two-device tip, the optional pre-reading (listed on the setup page), and – if GO – the extended-universe opt-in text.
- [ ] Confirm the deck's Multi100 slide against the registered protocol at osf.io/7snkz (the note on that slide asks for the registration's actual wording, not a paraphrase).

## The night before

- [ ] Render the full site: `quarto render` from the workspace root; check no errors; push; confirm the Pages build completes on GitHub Actions.
- [ ] **Live results loop** (full setup + checks in `facilitator/live-results-setup.md`): submit one anonymous test row via the Form (incognito), confirm it reaches the Sheet, confirm the Worker returns the sheet as CSV, press *Run Code* on the live [Multiverse]({{< var live-results-url >}}) page and see the test dot. Then delete the test row.
- [ ] **Prereg block loop**: open the workspace zip fresh (download it as a participant would), complete the declaration block with a dummy spec, render, and check the rendered block and timestamp. If the mirror form exists, submit one dummy row and delete it.
- [ ] **Browser lab cold load**: open `exercise/browser-lab.qmd`'s live page in a private window on the venue-typical connection; time the webR engine load; run the first chunk and the Task 3 reproduce chunk (t = −3.804).
- [ ] Confirm both OSF nodes load logged-out: osf.io/6zqct (fork) and osf.io/8rtwe (archive); confirm osf.io/h7432 shows the replication component (the scavenger target).
- [ ] Prepare the catch-up card, the help doc, and the day-plan message (texts below) as ready-to-paste snippets.
- [ ] Charge everything; second device signed in to Teams as a participant-view check.

## Open the room 30 minutes early {#opening-the-virtual-room--30-minutes-before}

- [ ] Open the Teams meeting early; enable chat for everyone; check breakout rooms are available (they are optional – nothing depends on them).
- [ ] Seed the chat: site URL · browser-lab URL · cheatsheet URL · the timestamped day plan (the standing order if the host drops: "follow the day plan; finish the current task or take the break early; I will rejoin").
- [ ] Post the interaction key: "green circle emoji = working · STUCK = I need help · answers to quizzes: type but hold until I say go".
- [ ] Share the deck; keep three tabs ready to switch: the deck, the spec menu, the Multiverse page.
- [ ] If recording: announce it now and state what is and is not recorded.

## Run sheet

Times in the block tables are block-relative: 0:00 is the start of that block. The clock below maps them onto the next delivery.

| Segment | Romanian time (EEST) | UK time (BST) |
|---|---|---|
| Block 1 – One paper, three verdicts | 10:00–11:30 | 08:00–09:30 |
| Break | 11:30–12:00 | 09:30–10:00 |
| Block 2 – The question underneath | 12:00–13:30 | 10:00–11:30 |
| Lunch | 13:30–14:30 | 11:30–12:30 |
| Block 3 – Preregister like an analyst | 14:30–16:00 | 12:30–14:00 |
| Break | 16:00–16:30 | 14:00–14:30 |
| Block 4 – Reading the multiverse | 16:30–18:00 | 14:30–16:00 |

You are two hours behind the room all day: the room's 10:00 start is your 08:00. Everything you post in chat should carry the Romanian clock, because that is the one the summer school published.

## Only the interaction layer swaps {#online--in-person-cue-sheet}

The materials are identical in both rooms. What changes is the mechanics of answering, of flagging trouble and of pairing up – so the table below is a swap list, not a second plan.

| Beat | Online (Teams) | In person |
|---|---|---|
| Quiz / waterfall answers | type in chat, hold until "go" | write on paper, hands up on "go" (or Vevox if the venue has it) |
| Working / stuck status | green-circle emoji / "STUCK" in chat | green / red-orange sticky notes |
| Roll-call | Teams "raise hand" | visual sweep |
| Pair moments | breakout rooms if available; scripted chat variant otherwise | table pairs |
| Rescues | buddy-chunk on the shared screen | facilitator circulates |
| The live chart | everyone opens the Multiverse page themselves | projector + own laptops |
| Form links | pasted in chat | QR codes on the slides |
| Breaks | countdown slide + "back at :xx" in chat | countdown slide + verbal |
| Facilitator absent | published day plan = standing order | n/a |

## Chat runs on protocol {#chat-protocols-and-ready-to-paste-texts}

**Waterfall:** "Type your answer now but DON'T send – hold it. … Go." Holding the answers back keeps each one independent of the others, and releasing them together is what produces the wall-of-identical-values beats.

**Help:** a STUCK in chat is the first flag. The standing **help doc** – a shared editable doc whose link goes into the chat at open – is the second surface, and the place errors get pasted. Check it at the minutes the run sheet names, not continuously. Rescues run in the main room by buddy-chunk: their spec, my webR or Positron, and everyone watching learns from it.

**Silent room:** wait 20 seconds, then take reactions (thumbs) as the minimal response, and name one or two people gently ("Sam, what did you get?"). Two substantive answers from twenty participants is a proceed, not a failure.

**Catch-up card (paste at Block 3 re-entry):**

> Just back? You missed nothing you can't recover: (1) if Task 4 (Estimand and DAG) is unfinished, run its DAG chunk as-is and come back to the wording later; (2) open the spec menu and pick ONE deviation; (3) when the room preregisters, complete the block and type "declared" like everyone else. Flag STUCK and I'll come to you in the run window.

**Facilitator-drop standing order (seeded in chat at open):**

> If I drop off the call: keep going. The day plan (link) has the timings – finish the current task or take the break early. I will rejoin as soon as I can.

## Cut in this order {#compression-ladders-with-trigger-times}

- **Block 1** – trigger 0:28: cut the Miske moderators slide to one line. Trigger 1:05 (hands-on dragging): the Task 3 fit becomes follow-my-screen for the stragglers; the waterfall still happens.
- **Block 2** – trigger ~1:05 (running long after estimands): the DAG crash course drops the spurious-by-design slide (one sentence instead) and reaches the half-built graph sooner. Trigger 1:15: Task 4 to demo-only (the v1-proven variant) – run it on my screen, they note the output and finish over lunch. The estimand waterfall is never compressed.
- **Block 3** – trigger 0:20: the spec menu drops to one worked example instead of two. The prereg moment and the run window are never compressed.
- **Block 4** – trigger 0:55: inference module leans on the reading (two slides instead of four); the git sketch to a pointer. The class-chart debrief and the fork-importance reveal are never compressed.

**Never cut:** the five-analyst reveal · the estimand waterfall · the half-built DAG and its adjustment set · the preregistration moment · results submission + the live chart debrief · the fork-importance reveal.

## Nothing here stops the day {#contingency-table}

Each row names the first move, not the only one, and every ladder ends somewhere the session can carry on from.

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| **A participant's webR fails mid-task** | The cheatsheet ladder: hard reload + rerun chunks above → second browser → buddy-chunk on my screen → grid lookup + hand submission (any spec looks up in `data/spec_grid_full.csv`, the full 2,520-row universe). Everyone lands a dot. |
| **Route 1 machine breaks** | Switch to the browser lab (full parity); their workspace survives for later. |
| **The live chart fails during the day** (Form, Worker, CORS) | Rung 1: `results.qmd` falls back to the committed `data/class_results.csv` automatically. Rung 2: pull the Sheet CSV, commit, re-render locally, share my screen. Rung 3: the static 840-spec curve + five-analyst slides still carry the debrief. Submissions are safe in the Sheet regardless – nothing upstream blocks on the chart. |
| **Breakout rooms unavailable** | Every pair moment has a scripted chat variant. Zero structural cost. |
| **OSF slow/unreachable during the scavenger** | Show h7432 on my screen; the beat survives. Data never depends on OSF live – it ships with both routes. |
| **My connection drops** | The standing order in chat: participants continue the current task or break early; I rejoin. The pipeline keeps collecting – it is entirely independent of the call. |
| **A participant cannot speak/hear** | Everything essential is chat-and-screen; deliver any spoken instruction in chat on request. |
| **Recording objections** | Recording is optional by design – stop it; nothing depends on it. |
| **Prereg mirror form fails** | The rendered block is the record; carry on. |

## Know these numbers cold {#answer-keys-and-expected-numbers}

- Warm-up matrix question set: 1 = reproducibility (a failed attempt is still reproducibility) · 2 = the grey area between reproducibility and robustness – argue both ways · 3 = replicability · 4 = generalisability.
- Task 3 (both routes): b = −0.00347, SE = 0.00091, **t = −3.804**, df = 233, N = 270 (`EUframes_cy.csv`) – the value on record for C6HJR, reproduced directly from `euframes`.
- The data-preparation material is off the running order and out of the deck. If you want to raise it on the day, the facts, the withdrawn slides and their speaker notes are in `_planning/block2-error-story-withdrawn-2026-07-30.md`, local to your machine – paste any block straight back into the deck.
- Family axis (a first-class menu axis; not part of Multi100's Task-2 menu, which fixed unemployment and, implicitly, the gaussian scale): beta submissions report **z**, not t. In the browser lab every spec, beta included, is read from the pre-computed grid, so `report_result()` takes no fit; Route 1 fits beta live. Grid-lookup fallback: any spec looks up in `data/spec_grid_full.csv` (the full universe of 2,520 rows), with `data/spec_grid_family.csv` (the family universe of 1,680 rows = the 840 Gaussian rows + their beta twins) as its family-only sibling. Beta twin of the anchor: b(logit) = −0.01399, **z = −4.075**, r = −0.258 (Gaussian anchor r = −0.242: same direction, still significant, slightly stronger).
- Claim-alignment (the room's convention, set on the spec menu): negative framings (`mcomm`, `mlib`, `mneg`) reverse-coded 1 − y before fitting; sign of b, t and r flips, magnitudes and p untouched (exactly so for beta too). Aligned r runs **−0.70 to +0.24** (gaussian; beta reaches +0.29) – so a class dot above ≈ +0.25 is almost certainly an **un-recoded negative framing**, not a genuine contrary result; name that in the debrief. One caveat from the growth-predictor axis: legitimately aligned growth-predictor dots can reach ≈ +0.37 – check the declared spec before calling it.
- Analyst placement (share of grid more negative, claim-aligned): KEVF1 15.8% · KQXUE 21.5% · C6HJR 49.6% · 018OL 63.1% · PRL47 67.9%. The two person-level analysts (KEVF1, PRL47) sit at the extremes; the constrained baseline lands almost exactly at the aligned grid's median.
- Task-1 layer (slide after analyst placement): free phase = five different questions – 018OL GDP p.c. level, KEVF1 growth, PRL47 a GDP battery; only KQXUE and C6HJR used unemployment – with one shared recorded verdict ('evidence for the claim'). No standardised Task-1 effect sizes exist in the public Multi100 data (verdict + free text only). My own Task 1 (`mposframe ~ growth + unemp`, two-way FE, World Bank series) reproduces from the committed as-submitted panel: unemployment t = −4.72, growth ns – standardisation *weakened* my result.
- Predictor axis (a first-class menu axis; menu + lab lookup, `spec_grid_full.csv`, full universe 2,520 = the family universe of 1,680 + growth 840, both families; not part of Multi100's Task-2 menu, though Task 1 shows three of five analysts freely chose GDP measures): GDP growth as claim carrier, raw form only – affine forms are t-inert (centred≡raw, log-z≡log), which is why the deduplicated canon holds 840 distinct analyses. Growth predictor (840 rows in the full grid): 70.5% claim-direction / 46.9% significant, aligned max +0.37 – direction without significance, matching KQXUE's Task-1 growth null. Growth mirror of my Task-1 model on the EU-frames panel: b = +0.00167, t = 1.59, ns. Growth polarity: claim-aligned reporting flips the sign (lab lookup does it).
- Fork importance: outcome 49.7% · residual/interactions 49.2% · sample 0.7 · estimator 0.4 · predictor form/copredictor/weights ≈ 0.
- Sign flips (mcosmo universe, 140 specs): 41 wrong-sign; 33 in `pooled_cl`, 8 in `fe_twoway`; 24 of the 41 in bailout-excluding samples (halved from the pre-dedupe counts – every distinct analysis appeared exactly twice before, so shares are invariant).
- Constrained universe: 140 specs · 70.7% negative · 57.1% negative-and-significant. Discussion-beat target: "no verdict without a null for dependent specifications – that is what a curve-level permutation test would supply (the design in the inference reading)."
- Baseline percentile (for participants without their own submission): −3.804 ⇒ ≈ 49.6% on the claim-aligned scale.

## Ask four to six of these {#debrief-question-bank}

Choose by what the class chart actually shows, not by the order below.

1. **Sign flip:** "Did anyone's specification flip the sign? If not – after seeing the flips chart, where would you have had to stand in the menu to flip it?"
2. **Significance loss:** "Did any spec lose significance? Reason to doubt the claim, or to scrutinise that spec?"
3. **Axis that moved most:** "Before I showed the decomposition – which axis did you bet on, and why did most of us get it wrong?"
4. **Justification quality:** "Whose DAG settled their choice? Whose DAG could have justified three different specs equally well?"
5. **Preregistration felt:** "Did completing the block before running change how the result felt when it landed? Would you have chosen differently after seeing it?"
6. **Robustness tolerance:** "Multi100 used ±0.05 and ±0.20 d. Is the claim robust by the tight standard here? The loose one? Who gets to choose the tolerance for a policy claim?"
7. **Against the five analysts:** "The class overlaps the five analysts' range. Is that reassuring or circular? What would a result *outside* their range have meant?"
8. **Percentile literacy:** "Your percentile places you among 840 defensible alternatives. What does a 10th-percentile analyst owe their reader that a 50th-percentile analyst does not?"
9. **The three Rs on one paper:** "This paper failed reproduction, survived robustness in sign but not magnitude, and sign-flipped in replication. Which R should worry us most – and does it depend on what the finding is used for?"
10. **The inference gap:** "If a curve-level permutation test came back at p = .30, what would survive of today? What if it came back at p = .004?"

## After the session

- [ ] Run the reset procedure from the top of this guide: export + commit the date-stamped snapshot, rotate the Sheet rows.
- [ ] Export the feedback form responses.
- [ ] Improvement log – record: which segment ran longest; did the estimand idea land (could people write one, did the waterfall show real spread); did Block 2's extra room let the DAGs breathe or expose thin material; how many declarations before the proceed rule fired; did every participant land a dot (which ladder rungs fired); did webR hold on home connections; Teams frictions (chat scale, breakouts, share switching).
